description:
FILED s473w (Opus, 2026-09-09) from the #1502 CPAN-board census.  WHOLE-FILE
LOSS, the #418/#419 family: one unreadable token and the reader never gets to
the rest of the file.

An `@ISA` parent whose CL package is never created makes the emitted file
UNREADABLE.  `Pl/Parser2.pm`'s MRO re-declaration emits

    (p-defclass TestExporter1::plc-testexporter1 (Exporter::plc-exporter) ())

for `our @ISA = ('Exporter')`, and nothing ever emits `(p-defpackage
:Exporter)`.  SBCL's READER â which consumes the whole top-level form before
anything runs â then dies

    read error during load:  Package Exporter does not exist.
      Line: 90, Column: 70, File-Position: 3632

and the file produces no TAP at all: the board records FAIL 0/0 where perl
gives 5 rows.

REPRODUCE (two board files, both Role-Tiny):

    tools/run-dist-t.pl ~/.cpan/build/Role-Tiny-2.002004-0 t/proto.t
      -> "Package Exporter does not exist"        (perl: 5/0)
    tools/run-dist-t.pl ~/.cpan/build/Role-Tiny-2.002004-0 t/extend-role-tiny.t
      -> "Package Role::Tiny does not exist"      (perl: 1/0)

and the emission alone, without SBCL:

    perl -I. -I~/.cpan/build/Role-Tiny-2.002004-0/t/lib \
         -I~/.cpan/build/Role-Tiny-2.002004-0/lib \
         ./pl2cl --no-cache --lenient-ppi \
         ~/.cpan/build/Role-Tiny-2.002004-0/t/proto.t | grep -n 'plc-exporter'

WHY THE TWO SPELLINGS DIFFER: `Exporter` is a package the program never
defines (it is core perl's, and PCL has no `lib/Exporter.pm` â its `import` is
handled elsewhere); `Role::Tiny` IS a real module, but the parent's package is
referenced in a form the reader reaches before the module's own
`p-defpackage` has been read.  Either way the rule is the same and it is the
one `reference_in_package_is_read_time` states: **a QUALIFIED symbol may only
name a package the reader has already created**, so every package named in an
emitted qualified symbol needs its `(p-defpackage â¦)` emitted ABOVE it â or
the class parent must be resolved at RUN time (`p-defclass` already takes the
parent by name elsewhere; check which spelling is the general one).

SIZE: unknown, but the failure mode is the expensive one â a whole file, not a
row, and silent about the cause unless someone reads the SBCL error.


=== s496 (Fable, 2026-09-25): a SMALLER reproducer, found by a review probe on main 9f6fe591 -- the parent package IS created, but too late for the READER because the whole BEGIN block is ONE top-level form:
    BEGIN { package Cfg; our @ISA = ("Exporter"); require Exporter; }  print "ok\n";     # perl: ok; PCL: read error "Package Exporter does not exist" (the (p-defclass Cfg::plc-cfg (Exporter::plc-exporter) ()) is READ before the require RUNS)
    package Cfg; BEGIN { our @ISA = ("Exporter") } package main; print "ok\n";          # same
    package Cfg; our @ISA = ("Exporter"); package main; print "ok\n";                   # OK (top level: each statement is its own top-level form)
    { package Cfg; our @ISA = ("Exporter"); }  print "ok\n";                            # OK (a bare block)
    use Exporter; BEGIN { package Cfg; our @ISA = ("Exporter"); ... }                   # OK (the package exists before the form is read)
  The `require`-inside-the-same-BEGIN order is common in test files that build a package inline (`BEGIN { package X; our @ISA = ("Exporter"); require Exporter; our @EXPORT = ...; $INC{"X.pm"} = 1 } use X;`).  The fix direction the task already names (do not depend on the parent package at READ time: a string/keyword superclass designator resolved at LOAD, or intern the package name in the emitting form) covers this shape too.  Probe files: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s496/isa-read{,2,3,4}.pl.
